intro: The paper studies executed contact-rich behavior across surface scanning, peg insertion, and fixed-stance humanoid interaction. The original results retain both successful and failed conditions, separate safe completion from raw completion, and evaluate the learned proposal prior through controlled simulation ablations.

figures.title: Progress must remain contact-valid
figures.alt: Original MGA surface-scanning results with hybrid-path coverage across eight methods, raw force and stiffness traces, and soft-curved-surface path error with and without local residual correction.
figures.caption: Hybrid contact coverage, force–stiffness response, and local residual correction (LRC). In the matched curved-soft-surface execution, MGA covers 96.0% of the path versus 50.5% without LRC while remaining within the 5 mm path tolerance. These panels show representative simulated executions; the table aggregates seeds.

figures.title: Safe completion is a separate outcome
figures.alt: Original stacked outcome bars for eight methods in nominal, pose-mismatch, and sensing-mismatch peg insertion. Safe completion, unsafe completion, and incomplete trials are shown separately for ten seeds per condition.
figures.caption: All ten seeds per method and insertion condition are retained. Across ID, Pose-OOD, and Sensing-OOD, MGA completes 28 of 30 trials safely; the two unsafe completions occur under pose mismatch. The plot distinguishes safe completion, completion with a wrench violation or jam, and incomplete insertion.

figures.title: Balance, contact, and object motion together
figures.alt: Original MGA humanoid results showing 15 N force regulation, fixed-stance box pushing, unjamming, and ten paired position–yaw trajectories with safety-triggered stops marked for the no-LRC ablation.
figures.caption: Simulated force regulation, fixed-stance pushing, and unjamming. The ten paired position–yaw trajectories expose continued interaction: MGA safely completes 10/10 unjamming trials, versus 3/10 without LRC. Crosses mark safety-triggered stops. Walking pushes are outside this reported comparison.

tables.title: Contact-rich simulation benchmarks
tables.caption: Complete main-results table: safe-success rate S (%) and normalized contact-load tail risk F (nCVaR95) across three contact-rich tasks.
notes: Entries are mean ± standard deviation over ten seeds. Surface-scanning groups contain four Hard, four Soft, three Hybrid, and two Unseen conditions; the groups are disjoint.

S uses task-specific safe-success criteria. Scanning requires at least 90% contact-valid coverage within 5 mm, at most 10% settled contact loss, and permits at most one of 100 force samples to exceed 60 N.

Peg-insertion safe success requires a complete 64-step execution without any wrench violation or jam, including after first completion. ID is nominal; Pose-OOD perturbs socket pose; Sensing-OOD biases wrench observations. Safety uses true simulated loads.

F is dimensionless normalized load-tail risk. Scanning and humanoid force are normalized by a 60 N limit; peg insertion uses the maximum normalized axial/lateral force and bending/torsional torque utilization. Lower loads alone do not imply completion.

† and ‡: Unjamming tails without the prior and without LRC are conditional on eight and three accepted runs, respectively; rejected prefixes count as failures. These tails are not ranked against the ten-run MGA estimate.

The prior is evaluated additively in peg insertion and the reported humanoid runs: one deterministic and eight stochastic learned horizons compete with the refined Gaussian sequence. This is not an equal-total-rollout-cost comparison with the no-prior ablation.

Humanoid results cover 15 N force regulation, a nominal 8 kg box pushed 0.10 m from fixed stance, and 0.03 m unjamming with yaw correction. Walking pushes and randomized pushing conditions are not in this comparison.
These are results of the paper protocol, separate from V1 GPU qualification and robot-controller deployment support.

tables.title: Repeated surface scanning on physical hardware
tables.caption: Original repeated-trial force measurements from a 6-DoF Dobot Nova 5 with wrist force/torque sensing. The hardware experiment evaluates the model-based component without a learned proposal prior.
notes: Mean ± sample standard deviation over five trials per surface. Statistics use unsmoothed, gravity-compensated and tared feedback with physical timestamps, including holds and recovery intervals during scanning.

All 15 scans reach their path endpoint. Complete-session outcomes are 5/5 for table, 4/5 for foam, and 5/5 for phantom; one foam session stops because robot feedback becomes stale after scanning and release.
The force calibration has a held-out 95th-percentile residual of 1.14 N. These metrics characterize compensated feedback rather than independently verified absolute contact force.

The hardware protocol uses a 0.4 s horizon, 48 candidate sequences, nominal 10 Hz planning and 20 Hz position commands, with bounded normal-force feedback. Results reflect the planner and feedback controller together.
